subject: Prompt & output governance safeguards for regulated pilot
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cedarhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Cedar Health Procurement <procurement@cedarhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot contract: governance around prompts & outputs

Marcus —

Thanks for the pilot proposal. Before we proceed, Legal and Security asked me to clarify two things that are blockers for the pilot kick-off:

1) We need a firm commitment that Cedar Health tenant data will not be used to improve or retrain any public or internal models (no adaptive training). Is Redwood able to provide a contractual "no-training" guarantee for the pilot environment?

2) For regulated PHI workflows we need clear ownership and exportability for generated outputs (prompts -> responses). Our counsel expects a description of how output ownership is handled and whether Redwood will assert any derivative rights. We also need to understand subprocessor access to both prompts and generated outputs.

I attached our draft DPA with inline redlines — please review. Procurement is copied for contract cadence.

Elena
Elena Soto
Director, Product Compliance — Cedar Health
Attachments: CedarHealth_DPA_annotated.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot contract: governance around prompts & outputs

Elena —

Thanks for the clear note and the redlined DPA. High level answers below; I included Priyom (sales ops) and Laura (privacy/product) to confirm and draft appropriate contract language.

1) No-training guarantee: Yes — for the pilot we can commit to an enforceable contractual clause that Redwood will not use Cedar Health data to further train or fine-tune any models. We provide operational isolation for pilot tenants (separate project IDs, disabled telemetry for model updates, and an audit trail). We can supply an evidence pack (ops logs + configuration) at the end of each month.

2) Output ownership & derivative rights: Redwood policy is to grant customers full rights to outputs generated from their inputs. We will not claim derivative ownership over prompt->response outputs for Cedar Health. We propose text that (a) confirms customer ownership of outputs, (b) disclaims Redwood ownership of derivatives generated from customer-supplied prompts, and (c) limits Redwood use of outputs to deliver the service only (no indexing, no model improvement).

3) Subprocessors: Our typical model is to list subprocessors in the DPA appendix and to require onshore routing for pilot workloads if needed. For Cedar Health we can gate any subprocessor that would see prompts/outputs — we will include an explicit subprocessors annex and offer a 30-day notification + approval right for any new subprocessor during the pilot.

Next steps: Laura and I will propose redline language for sections 4 (Model improvement), 7 (Outputs & IP), and Annex B (Subprocessors). Can you confirm Procurement's timeline for signature and whether you need an operational evidence sample before PO?

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cedarhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot contract: governance around prompts & outputs

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. A couple of operational clarifications that Procurement usually requests so we can mirror them in the SOW/Order Form:

- Evidence cadence: We can provide a monthly evidence bundle (audit logs of data flow, disabled telemetry settings, subprocessors list snapshot). Is monthly sufficient or do you require weekly artifacts for the pilot?
- Onshore routing: We can route all Cedar Health pilot requests to our us-east region and enforce onshore KMS usage for keys. That will be added as a control in Annex B.
- Escrow/escrow alternative: If Legal insists on an escrow of model state to prove non-learning, we can propose an operational proof-of-non-training workflow (ops logs + continuous KV snapshot) rather than code escrow. Does your counsel prefer a technical snapshot or a contractual audit right?

I'll attach a short playbook that describes the operational proof-of-no-training flow we use with other regulated partners.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-proof-no-train-playbook.md
From: Cedar Health Procurement <procurement@cedarhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cedarhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 11:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot contract: governance around prompts & outputs

Marcus/Priyom —

Procurement here. Our counsel responded to the high-level assurances and asked for two additions to the DPA that will be required prior to countersignature:

1) A clause that explicitly prohibits Redwood from retaining prompt/response content beyond the pilot's agreed retention window unless explicitly authorized in writing. The draft DPA included a retention schedule; counsel wants a hard cap and an automatic data deletion certificate upon termination of the pilot.

2) For the subprocessors annex, counsel wants a commitment that any subprocessor with access to outputs will either be onshore or will sign a binding no-training addendum. If a subprocessor cannot sign that addendum, Redwood must route requests away from that subprocessor for Cedar Health traffic.

Also, counsel asked whether Redwood can provide a short operational sample (redacted) proving the evidence artifact that would be delivered monthly. If you can provide that sample we can evaluate acceptance faster.

Procurement target: counter-signature in 2 weeks subject to acceptance of the deletion certificate wording and subprocessors control.

Thanks,
Cedar Health Procurement
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Cedar Health Procurement <procurement@cedarhealth.com>, Elena Soto <elena.soto@cedarhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot contract: governance around prompts & outputs

Hi Elena / Procurement —

Thanks for the clarity — below are concrete proposals we will include in the updated DPA and pilot SOW. We aim to send redlines by end of day tomorrow.

A) Retention & deletion: Add a "Data Retention & Deletion Certificate" clause to the DPA: Redwood will enforce the agreed retention schedule, and within 7 calendar days of pilot termination we will provide a signed deletion certificate plus a summary of deletion artifacts (deleted object ids, snapshot nonce). Operationally we will disable backups for the tenant and run the deletion job in our US region.

B) Subprocessor access control: Annex B will list current subprocessors and include a binding "No-Training Addendum" template. For any new subprocessor, Redwood will either (i) obtain a signed no-training addendum from the subprocessor prior to access, or (ii) route Cedar Health traffic to an alternate onshore worker pool that excludes that subprocessor. We will also provide a 30-day notice window for any subprocessor changes.

C) Evidence sample: I attached a redacted monthly evidence sample and a short scopesheet that maps proof artifacts to DPA sections. Please review and confirm if it satisfies counsel's requirements.

Action items:
- Marcus / Priyom: finish contract redlines for sections called out by Elena and Procurement.
- David (ops): prepare redacted evidence sample for today's attachment.
- Elena / Procurement: confirm whether 7-day deletion certificate timing is acceptable.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product & Privacy — Redwood Inference
Attachments: pilot-scopesheet.xlsx
